land.text: the southern part of the Byzantine province of Sardinia, governed from Cagliari by a magistrate after the conquest of 534; infobox Preceded by: Byzantine Empire

predecessors.note: The page says the founding date is unknown; local judges gradually became de facto independent from the early 8th century. 866 is Cliopatria's year.

land.text: Pisa kept control of Castel di Castro; the Della Gherardesca third is listed here because the infobox names the Republic of Pisa as a successor (the page names the family, not the state)

successors.note: One of three parts of the territory after 1258; the page does not say which.

land.text: one of the three parts into which the territory was divided, assigned to Arborea

successors.note: Which part is not on the page.

land.text: one of the three parts, assigned to Gallura

successors.note: Which part is not on the page. The infobox lists only Pisa and Arborea as successors; the article text names Gallura.

capitals.name: Santa Igia (near Cagliari)
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Santa Igia. 'Starting from the 9th century AD, it became the seat of the giudice' (Santa Igia page); Cagliari itself was abandoned in the 8th-9th century after pirate raids. Coordinates are approximate (the north shore of the Santa Gilla lagoon), not from the page.

keyframe_review.note: unverified for 866-910: the page says the founding date is unknown (infobox Established: 1020) and the History of Sardinia page has the judicates appear 'from the mid-11th century'; but Santa Igia was the giudice's seat 'from the 9th century', so a southern Sardinian state under a giudice in 866 is plausible. 10,190 km2; the page gives no area (no infobox figure to compare). Soft.
As the 866 shape: 10,263 km2, no infobox area to compare. The page names thirteen curatoriae and no boundary, so the outline stands as Cliopatria's approximation.

correction.text: Cliopatria's reduced 1015 shape (the judicate without the southern coastal plain that Mujahid occupied), for 1015-1016 only; from 1017 the 1018 shape applies

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria cuts the south and leaves 2,647 km2 of 10,263 for 1015-1017. The Mujahid page says he occupied 'the southern coastal plain' in 1015 and, returning in 1016, beat the army of the judge of Cagliari before fleeing in May 1016 with his fleet wrecked; so the reduced shape holds for 1015-1016 only and the full shape returns in 1017. The cut-out is the occupied land (ledger: occupation 1015-1016).
10,263 km2. Applies from 1017 (see the 1015 verdict): Mujahid left Sardinia in 1016 and nothing in the pages opened changes the judicate's land until 1258. No infobox area.
Same outline as the 1018 shape (10,263 km2): Cliopatria splits the row at 1177 with no change of area. The row ends 1187 but the judicate did not: see the 1188 keyframe.

correction.text: the 1177 shape carried forward to 1258: the judicate under the House of Massa, whose last giudice William III was deposed when Santa Igia fell

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria drops the judicate after 1187, probably reading the 1188 change of house ('In 1188, Cagliari was conquered by the House of Massa from the Republic of Pisa', History of Sardinia page) as the end. The Cagliari page has William I ruling 1188-1214, Benedetta 1214-1232 and William III 1256-1258, so the judicate lasted to 1258 on the same land.

region.text: the southern part of Sardinia, divided into thirteen curatoriae

ledger.note: 866: the Judicate of Cagliari appears in Cliopatria's first shape, under a giudice at Santa Igia; the page dates no founding. It says the founding date is unknown, though the infobox gives 1020 as the year established; it is silent on 866, so this is bridging.

region.text: 'the southern coastal plain' that Mujahid occupied (Mujahid page); drawn as the part Cliopatria cuts from the judicate in 1015-1017

ledger.note: 1015: Mujahid of Denia lands in Sardinia with 120 ships and occupies the southern coastal plain. Mujahid launched an expedition 'to conquer the island of Sardinia' in 1015 (AH 406); the Taifa of Denia holds the land, the judicate keeps the rest. The page names no district beyond 'the southern coastal plain'; the region is Cliopatria's cut-out.

region.text: 'the southern coastal plain' that Mujahid occupied (Mujahid page); drawn as the part Cliopatria cuts from the judicate in 1015-1017

ledger.note: 1016: Mujahid flees Sardinia and Pisan and Genoese fleets capture what is left of his ships. He came back in 1016, beat the army of the judge of Cagliari and fortified the conquered area, but, facing mutiny, he fled by sea in May 1016. The page's May 1016 sentence is garbled; the year is clear, the month follows it.

1188: Pisa installs the House of Massa at Cagliari; William I rules 1188-1214. Pisa sent Obert, Margrave of Massa, to take the judicate; William I, son of Obert and a daughter of Constantine II, ruled from 1188 to 1214 (History of Sardinia page: 'In 1188, Cagliari was conquered by the House of Massa from the Republic of Pisa'). The state, its land and its colour continue.

region.text: Gallura, the judicate of Elena, invaded in 1206

ledger.note: 1206: William I of Cagliari invades Gallura. Gallura page: in 1206 William I of Cagliari invaded Elena's judicate; the Cagliari page adds that William failed to conquer Gallura, which was defended by Lamberto Visconti. The page names no district, so the zone is Gallura's whole shape.

region.text: Gallura, the judicate of Elena, invaded in 1206

ledger.note: 1207: Lamberto Visconti marries Elena of Gallura and repulses the Cagliari invasion. In 1207 she married the Pisan Lamberto Visconti, who repulsed the invasion (Gallura page). The repulse is dated by the marriage year.

region.text: Santa Igia and the territory of the judicate, besieged and conquered by the Pisans and their Sardinian allies

ledger.note: 1258: Pisa and the other judicates besiege Santa Igia. Pisa and the other judicates attacked and besieged Santa Igia, and Cagliari lost the war; the siege is not dated apart from the year the judicate ended. In 1256 John had tried to throw off the Pisan yoke by allying with Genoa and was assassinated by Pisan agents; William III succeeded.

region.text: Santa Igia and the territory of the judicate, besieged and conquered by the Pisans and their Sardinian allies

ledger.note: 1258: the last battle is lost and the contest ends with the judicate's fall. Same year as the siege; the page gives no separate date for the end of the fighting.

region.text: the whole judicate, divided into three parts plus Castel di Castro

ledger.note: 1258: Santa Igia falls and the Judicate of Cagliari is divided. In 1258 'the history of the giudicato came to a sudden close'; the territory was divided into three parts, assigned to the Della Gherardesca family, to Arborea and to Gallura, while Pisa kept control of Castel di Castro (Cagliari page; Santa Igia page: 'In 1258, during the process of conquest of the Giudicato of Cagliari' the city was destroyed). The pages do not say which third went to whom; month not given.

wars.name: Dénia invasion of Sardinia

zones.text: 'the southern coastal plain' that Mujahid occupied (Mujahid page); drawn as the part Cliopatria cuts from the judicate in 1015-1017

wars.outcome: Mujahid occupied the southern coastal plain in 1015, beat the judge of Cagliari's army in 1016 and fled in May 1016 when his men mutinied; a storm and the Pisan and Genoese fleets destroyed his ships.
wars.note: The Taifa of Denia page says only that the camp was 'in the north of the island for one year'; the two pages disagree about where the army sat (south here, north there).

wars.name: Cagliari's invasion of Gallura
wars.outcome: William I of Cagliari invaded Gallura in 1206 and failed; Lamberto Visconti, married to Elena in 1207, repulsed him.

wars.name: William I of Cagliari's wars
wars.outcome: William 'spent his reign (1188-1214) in constant wars with Arborea, Gallura, and Logudoro'; he imprisoned Peter I of Arborea and ruled Arborea in his name, but failed to conquer Gallura.
wars.note: No campaign other than the 1206 invasion of Gallura is dated, so no zone is drawn; the rule over Arborea in Peter's name has no dates on the page.

wars.name: Fall of the Judicate of Cagliari
wars.outcome: In 1256 John allied with Genoa against Pisa and was assassinated; William III succeeded; Pisa and the other judicates besieged Santa Igia in 1258 and the judicate was divided into three parts, Pisa keeping Castel di Castro.
wars.note: Genoa appears only as John's ally in 1256; the Santa Igia page names the Pisans and their Sardinian allies without listing them. Arborea, Gallura and Logudoro are listed from the Cagliari page's reference to the other judicates and need the Arborea dossier's confirmation.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page opened; the pages give curatoriae and cities only, and Cliopatria's outline follows modern provinces. The 1258 partition lines are not given at all.

notes: FOUNDING: Cliopatria starts the row in 866; the Cagliari page says the founding date is unknown and gives 1020 as the infobox 'Established' year, and the History of Sardinia page has the judicates appear 'from the mid-11th century'. The dossier keeps 866 (Cliopatria's year, with the seat at Santa Igia from the 9th century) at confidence 1; a gap-filler may prefer 1020. END: Cliopatria's last shape ends 1187; the page runs the judicate to 1258 (Santa Igia destroyed), so 1188-1258 is a new keyframe on the 1177 outline. PERSONAL UNION: the Cagliari page says Benedetta (judge 1214-1232) married Barisone III of Arborea, uniting the two judicates until his death in 1217; no territory event is written because an association is not territory (rule 4) and the marriage year is not given. PISAN SUPREMACY: the page has Cagliari under papal and Pisan authority in Torchitorio's reign and Constantine II pledging loyalty to the archbishop of Pisa (undated); no event is written. PARTITION 1258: three parts (Della Gherardesca, Arborea, Gallura) plus Pisa's Castel di Castro; the boundaries are not on any page opened (a gap for the Pisa/Arborea dossiers; the Della Gherardesca lordship is a Pisan fief, which the pages do not say). DENIA: the Taifa of Denia dossier (eu-12) records the Sardinian camp as 'the north of the island' with counterparts Gallura and Logudoro and none for Cagliari; this dossier follows the Mujahid page (southern coastal plain, army of the judge of Cagliari), so Denia's dossier needs an occupation of the south against giudicato-of-cagliari. RULERS: the page lists only Constantine I 1089-1102, William I 1188-1214, Benedetta 1214-1232 and William III 1256-1258, so no ruler strip is written. COORDINATES of Santa Igia are approximate. Budget: five pages, as allowed; Judicate of Arborea and Republic of Pisa were opened and gave nothing for Cagliari. No gazetteer name is needed.
